executiveSummary: GM0088 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but it is not a defensible Schiermonnikoog first-72-hour forecast. This isolated Wadden island has 971 registered residents, about 300,000 annual visitors, no road or rail connection, one regular ferry link through a dynamic tidal channel, off-island acute-care dependence, and drinking water supplied from its own vulnerable freshwater lens rather than a mainland pipe. Wetterskip Fryslân manages distinct 9.2-km sandy and 4.0-km Wadden Sea primary defences, while large eastern salt-marsh areas normally inundate at storm tide outside the protected core. The model instead has zero logical transport edges, applies an exact T+24 coastal legacy flood amplitude of 1.798438 and 610 affected people-equivalent without a selected water level, dune/dike failure or connected footprint, and generates exact service/recovery percentages without ferry, fresh-water, visitor, shelter, medical-evacuation or operator state. Eight active single hazards reuse the same two-neighbourhood order; canonical wildfire has zero direct fire despite an active seasonal smoking/fire ban across the extensive National Park. Official 2026 evidence says short-notice evacuation is nearly impossible and proposed high-ground shelter lacks electricity, running water, food and medical facilities. Unknown/NoData must never be presented as zero, safe, open or available; unsupported flood, transport, exposure, lifeline and recovery precision requires correction.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0088 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG place and neighbourhoods
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS table identifies GM0088 as Schiermonnikoog and reports 971 residents, density 23 per square kilometre, 31.4% aged 65 or older and 340 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [6.247085391425039, 53.491254987965206] lies inside the 2025 generalized multipolygon. The BAG Schiermonnikoog label point lies just outside the independently generalized boundary, while the one BRT woonkern remains Schiermonnikoog; this is an island/coastal generalization caveat, not proof of wrong assignment.

Two neighbourhood rows sum to 970 residents, one below the municipal total (-0.103%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 971. Registers omit tourists, seasonal workers, day visitors, ferry passengers, patients, responders and household preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Schiermonnikoog / Wetterskip Fryslân / Vitens / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: Current island water-safety, freshwater and climate-resilience programme
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; 1EILAUN cooperation signed 3 July 2025; no blanket page licence identified
supports: The municipality states that all island drinking water comes from a freshwater groundwater lens because there is no drinking-water pipeline to the island. The integral water plan addresses retaining rain without nuisance while sustaining drinking water, agriculture, nature, residents, recreation and tourism during dry periods.

The municipality, Wetterskip, Rijkswaterstaat, Vitens, Natuurmonumenten, farmers and province are planning dike and dune strengthening. Programme approval and cooperation are not completed protection, current defence condition, groundwater stock, treatment capacity or T+72 availability.

In May 2026 the municipality said it had begun mapping vital/vulnerable assets such as energy landing points, emergency-service sites and food locations, and that evacuation is nearly impossible while temporary island shelter is possible. Mapping/planning does not establish protected location, capacity or operational state.

The municipal climate page says extreme rainfall can inundate streets and homes. It supplies no event hyetograph, AHN/street-flow surface, sewer/infiltration capacity, groundwater level, resolution, licence or NoData for the simulator.

evidenceSources.title: Primary sandy/Wadden defences, water-control assets and outer-dike salt marsh
evidenceSources.edition: Wetterskip Waterveiligheid 2025; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; current nature pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Wetterskip's 2025 duty-of-care report distinguishes the 9.2-km sandy primary defence and 4.0-km Wadden Sea defence on Schiermonnikoog, each with published 1:1000 signal and lower-bound standards, and identifies an island discharge culvert. Standards and inspection governance are not breach probability for a selected event or live defence state.

Natuurmonumenten says much of the island is outer-dike and that lower salt-marsh and beach areas flood during hard northwesterly wind and spring tide. Normal outer-dike tidal/storm inundation must remain separate from failure of defences protecting the village/polder.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 23 GM0088 points: one sewer pump, one surface-water pump, one wastewater treatment point and 20 weirs. All 23 capacities are null; point type and manager do not establish hydraulic/sewer connectivity, operation, backup, condition or spare capacity.

A defensible direct-flood layer requires a selected RWS/Wetterskip/WMCN/LIWO source, water-level boundary and datum, wind/wave setup, defence or overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, edition, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData.

evidenceSources.title: Lauwersoog–Schiermonnikoog ferry, tidal channel and 2026 timetable
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages and WPD 2026 timetable inspected 3 September 2026; RWS network geometry available as public service; no blanket WPD page licence identified
supports: Rijkswaterstaat identifies the Wagenborg passenger ferry from Lauwersoog to Schiermonnikoog and maintains the tidal channel and ferry infrastructure; Rijksoverheid identifies it as the Waddenveren Oost concession. The WPD 2026 schedule runs through 4 January 2027.

Rijkswaterstaat reported substantial silting in the Glinder route, prior one-way vessel traffic, a 2025 channel realignment and continuing uncertainty because Wadden Sea morphology is difficult to predict. Historic work is not current disruption, but it demonstrates that maritime geometry and navigability matter.

The simulator contains zero logical transport edges for GM0088 even though 24 local GTFS stop areas include Veerdam. Local bus stops cannot substitute for the cross-water ferry, mainland road/rail connections, freight capacity or emergency marine/air transport.

Schedule and concession status do not establish weather/tide-dependent sailing, vessel/berth availability, freight and passenger capacity, medical priority, mainland onward route, supplies or recovery. Missing live state remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: National Park extent, visitor exposure, outer-dike landscape and seasonal fire controls
evidenceSources.edition: Current park pages and 2024 visitor plan/folder inspected 3 September 2026; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The National Park reports about 5,400 hectares, 18 km length, approximately 950 residents and approximately 300,000 visitors per year. Annual visitors are not concurrent incident occupancy, but prove that resident-only exposure can be materially incomplete.

The 2024 park plan says more than 80% of visitors primarily walk or cycle. Beaches, dunes, forest, salt marsh, camping and widely dispersed routes create hazard-specific presence and access that a two-neighbourhood resident allocation cannot resolve.

The official welcome folder imposes a complete smoking and open-fire ban outside the village from 1 April through 1 October because of fire danger; that control is active on the audit date. It establishes prevention and fuel concern, not an ignition, fire phase, perimeter or successful enforcement.

Park/nature pages establish eligible storm-tide, fire/smoke, search/rescue and visitor domains, but not event-time people, fuel moisture, ignition/spread, wind/plume, closures, firefighting water, responders or containment.

evidenceSources.title: Island crisis guidance, medical evacuation and external acute-care dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal/KNRM pages inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The municipality describes siren/radio warning, sheltering and special transport for people needing assistance, older people and pupils. It does not identify an activation, resource inventory, route, capacity, recipient list or completion state.

In January 2026 the municipality said short-notice pre-storm evacuation remains virtually impossible and high-ground shelter in dunes lacks electricity, running water, food and medical facilities; post-storm rescue to the mainland is constrained by limited rescue means and damaged infrastructure. This is current policy/risk evidence, not proof of a present incident.

KNRM Schiermonnikoog is callable 24/7 and public incident records demonstrate patient transport by rescue boat and helicopter in cooperation with ambulance/huisarts. First-party examples establish possible modes, not guaranteed availability, weather limits, medical capacity or T+72 throughput.

RIVM assigns no acute-care department to GM0088. Nearest straight-line reference-point locations are UMCG Groningen 37.183 km, Martini Groningen 38.972 km, Nij Smellinghe Drachten 44.521 km and Frisius MC Leeuwarden 44.555 km, all 24/7 in the annual register. These are not marine/air/ambulance travel times, live acceptance, capacity, staffing or access.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RWS Waterinfo / KNMI
evidenceSources.title: Public grid-planning, communications, education and bounded observation context
evidenceSources.edition: Public planning/register/observation snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: One postcode sample, 9166RB, maps to Liander OS DOKKUM 10-1i and reports withdrawal existing/required 22/18 MW, injection 22/25 MW, queue fields null, six projects and earliest year 2027. A mainland station-area planning sample is not island feeder/landing topology, municipal coverage, live load, outage, backup or restoration; its exact reuse licence was not identified.

RDI returns eight antenna sites: five mobile, one fixed-link, one amateur and one other-mobile. DUO returns three education records. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, satellite/radio fallback, occupants, shelter role, supplies or current operation; RDI cadence/licence is unstated and DUO is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified.

No GM0088 RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI observation/warning, NDW situation, public camera or acute-care point is assigned in the bounded deployment. These are source/spatial/temporal coverage facts, never normal water/weather, open transport, safe conditions or available care.
Public-context records remain affectsSimulation=false unless a reviewed causal adapter binds compatible topology, state, valid time and uncertainty.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM0088 is uniquely Schiermonnikoog in Fryslân and Veiligheidsregio Fryslân.
The municipal reference point is contained and no headline statistical mismatch was found.
The BAG label-point/generalized-boundary mismatch is retained as a geometry caveat, not silently snapped or excluded.

geography.summary: The island boundary is coherent, but protected core, outer-dike nature, dunes, dike and tidal water require full source geometry.
notes: One district and two large neighbourhoods cannot resolve village, Banckspolder, dunes, freshwater lens, beaches, forest, salt marsh, harbour/veerdam and eastern wilderness.
Normal storm-tide inundation of outer-dike salt marsh must remain separate from sandy/Wadden primary-defence failure affecting protected areas.
Every flood, nature, freshwater and vital-object layer needs publisher, edition, scenario, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and explicit NoData.

demography.summary: Resident totals reconcile, but seasonal visitor exposure can exceed the registered population and is absent.
notes: Population is 971, density 23, age65Pct 31.4 and one-person households 340. Neighbourhood rows sum to 970 (-1, -0.103%), households 585 and published age65+ 310.
Schiermonnikoog neighbourhood has 890 published residents and Verspreide huizen 80; exact allocation reconciles to 971.
Approximately 300,000 annual visitors are not an event-time count, but resident-only affected-population ceilings omit potentially material tourists, campers, workers and ferry queues.
No reviewed privacy-safe hourly/day-type presence range, accommodation occupancy or evacuation-assistance demand is integrated.

regionalDetail.summary: Most two-row statistics load, while infrastructure, visitor and operational states remain incomplete.
notes: Cars per household covers 1/2 neighbourhoods; district heating and public charging cover 0/2. Null is not zero.
All 23 HWH water capacities are null. One grid sample, eight antennas and three education records do not establish island-wide or incident-time availability.
Freshwater lens level/quality, Vitens abstraction/treatment, energy landing/feed, ferry freight, food/medicine/fuel stock, visitors and care state are absent.

settlements.summary: The one settlement is coherent, with a documented BAG label generalization mismatch.
notes: BAG and BRT both identify Schiermonnikoog, but the BAG label point lies outside the independently generalized CBS multipolygon.
Compare full-resolution source editions before any correction; do not snap, drop or treat the label as missing population.
A settlement label cannot establish tourists, dispersed nature users, shelter or supply role.

transport.summary: The simulator has no cross-boundary edge and therefore omits the island's ferry, maritime/air emergency and mainland onward dependencies.
notes: Logical route degree is zero, despite the official Lauwersoog–Schiermonnikoog ferry concession and RWS channel/terminal responsibility.
Twenty-four local GTFS stops include Veerdam, but local bus geometry cannot carry people, freight, fuel, medicine, repair crews or ambulances across the Wadden Sea.
Ferry timetable, channel, tide/weather, vessel/berth, freight/passenger/medical priority and Lauwersoog onward road state are missing; rescue boat/helicopter are distinct contingency modes.
Empty road/observation screens do not mean that travel is open or available.

emergencyContext.summary: Official shelter/evacuation constraints and island lifelines are identified, but no auditable first-72-hour state drives the model.
notes: Current municipal evidence says pre-storm evacuation is nearly impossible and high-ground shelter lacks basic utilities and medical facilities.
No full acute-care department is local; medical evacuation depends on huisarts/ambulance, KNRM or helicopter, weather/tide, transfer and mainland hospital acceptance.

Required first-72-hour categories include warning, tourist accounting, high-ground shelter, assisted transport, dune/dike action, freshwater protection/distribution, ferry/harbour state, medical evacuation, nature-fire response, food/fuel/medicine, energy/telecom repair and mainland mutual aid.
Plans, siren guidance, schedules and callable services are not confirmed resources, action completion or T+72 recovery.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: The mandatory gate covers severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

At T+24 severity / pressure / affected people-equivalent / event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.168320 / 0.349204 / 286 / 4,384.748; pluvial 0.180721 / 0.193473 / 73 / 2,603.555; river 0 / 0.044790 / 0 / 0; coastal 0.632207 / 0.585449 / 610 / 10,581.759; heat 0.117838 / 0.213951 / 101 / 2,912.977.
Affected people-equivalent is not observed people, casualties, evacuees or visitors; person-hours is cumulative weighted resident service shortfall against a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0088 pnpm audit:model passed both tests over the complete matrix.
Zero-event effects, repeatability, UI/core preset equality, local population/demand/delivery, hazard-layer invariance and burden monotonicity pass.
A zero-edge graph can satisfy numerical bounds while omitting the island's most important external lifeline. Arithmetic correctness does not establish calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Coastal depth and two-area ranking do not distinguish protected, outer-dike, freshwater, village and nature domains.
notes: Coastal T+24 reports legacy flood amplitude 1.798438 and 610 resident people-equivalent without selected North Sea/Wadden boundary, dune/dike breach/overtopping or connected footprint.

Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Verspreide huizen above Schiermonnikoog at T+24; compound repeats it. With only two huge polygons, exact ordering cannot resolve documented pathways.

Normal salt-marsh flooding, protected village/polder failure, dune high ground, fresh-water abstraction, ferry harbour and seasonal nature users require distinct polygons/objects and event-time presence.
River direct zero is scoped to that generic preset and cannot be interpreted as all inland/tidal flooding safe.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service values omit ferry, fresh-water, energy landing, visitor, shelter and medical-evacuation dependencies.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 0.361213, water 0.449933, drainage 0.277130, gas 0.661721, telecom 0.286834, mobility 0.428787, facilities 0.503259 and supply 0.366557; no operator or authority validates these decimals.
All local drinking water comes from the island freshwater lens, while the model has no abstraction/treatment/quality/reserve or emergency-distribution evidence.
A zero-edge network cannot model ferry-borne food, fuel, medicine, crews or mainland acute-care transfer; scheduled bus stops and callable KNRM do not guarantee operation.
HWH, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records remain non-causal context unless compatible topology/state is reviewed.

causalTrace.summary: Unresolved coastal, visitor, ferry, freshwater, fire and cyber dimensions are hidden behind exact output.
notes: Coastal direct impact lacks source boundary water level/datum, wind/wave setup, dune/dike condition, breach/overtopping state, footprint, arrival and recession; unsupported dimensions are not declared beside the exact depth/affected count.
Canonical wildfire has direct fire zero and synthetic smoke without ignition/perimeter, while cyber has no named target. A seasonal fire ban is prevention context, not incident state.
A legacy field named floodDepthM must not be presented as surveyed or forecast metres.

Dated defence standards, plans, current pages, schedules, public registers and synthetic T+72 output require distinct publisher/version/retrieval/issue/valid times, evidence class, coverage, licence and NoData.

recovery72h.summary: Coastal/compound residuals and generic recovery are unsupported by island access, shelter, lifeline or action evidence.
notes: Coastal direct severity/amplitude return to zero by T+72, yet 143 resident people-equivalent remain affected, pressure is 0.244807 and person-hours reach 33,028.112; availability remains as low as Telecom 0.596246 and Facilities 0.629823 without ferry, repair, shelter or dewatering state.

Compound worsens from T+24 to T+72: pressure 0.559381 to 0.603891, affected 574 to 635, Facilities 0.584848 to 0.346024 and person-hours to 34,819.048 while flood amplitude stays 0.339927. No documented action/resource explains it.

Storm/pluvial/winter/wildfire direct effects clear, cyber declines and earthquake/heat reach zero affected with exact residual services. Generic curves ignore weather/tide-dependent access, tourists, freshwater, high-ground shelter and external care.
The municipality explicitly warns that island shelter lacks utilities/medical support and post-storm rescue is complex; recovery must be action- and resource-driven rather than presumed at 72 hours.

findings.summary: The zero-edge transport graph omits Schiermonnikoog's sole regular mainland connection.
findings.evidence: The model has no route and no neighbour for GM0088, while RWS, Rijksoverheid and WPD identify the Lauwersoog ferry, tidal channel, ferry infrastructure and 2026 timetable. Twenty-four local stops include Veerdam but cannot represent the Wadden crossing, freight, medical transfer or mainland onward route.
findings.action: Add an authority-reviewed multimodal ferry edge with terminal/channel/vessel, timetable and valid departures, weather/tide/navigability, passenger/freight/vehicle/medical priority capacity, mainland road/rail transfer, disruption and recovery. Model KNRM/helicopter only as separately activated emergency modes; absent state is Unknown.

findings.summary: Exact coastal inundation lacks a selected Schiermonnikoog dune/dike or outer-dike case.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports legacy amplitude 1.798438 and 610 affected resident people-equivalent. Official evidence distinguishes sandy and Wadden Sea primary defences from salt-marsh/beach storm-tide inundation; no water level/datum, wind/waves, defence/breach/overtopping, connected footprint, arrival or recession selects the model result.
findings.action: Suppress exact direct coastal impact until an expert-selected, versioned Wetterskip/RWS/WMCN/LIWO case provides source boundary, defence state, footprint, depth/velocity, timing, probability, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Keep normal outer-dike flooding separate from protected-core failure and preserve Unknown rather than forcing zero.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure cannot support island evacuation, shelter or supply decisions.
findings.evidence: All affected counts are capped to 971 residents, while the National Park reports roughly 300,000 annual visitors and widespread walking/cycling/nature use. Annual visitors are not concurrent occupancy, but prove that tourists, campers, seasonal workers and ferry queues can materially change warning, shelter, water, food and medical demand.
findings.action: Keep CBS residents authoritative and add privacy-safe event-time/day-type visitor, accommodation, camping, ferry-arrival and workforce presence ranges with source, valid time and uncertainty. Never convert annual totals to concurrent people; show Unknown when current occupancy is unavailable.

findings.summary: Water availability ignores the island freshwater lens and has no mainland fallback topology.
findings.evidence: Official partners state that all tap water comes from the local freshwater lens because no drinking-water pipeline reaches the island. Coastal T+24 Water is exactly 0.449933 and later recovers without groundwater level/salinity, Vitens abstraction/treatment, storage, power, contamination, demand including visitors or emergency distribution evidence; all 23 HWH capacities are null.
findings.action: Model a protected aggregate freshwater source–treatment–storage–distribution dependency with authorized level/quality/abstraction, visitor-adjusted demand, power/backup and emergency water actions. If operational data are unavailable, use labelled ranges/Unknown and never infer capacity from HWH nulls.

findings.summary: The wildfire preset does not exercise the island's protected dune/forest fire pathway.
findings.evidence: At T+24 canonical wildfire has direct fire zero, smoke 0.141929, zero affected and 835.373 person-hours. The 5,400-hectare National Park has an active 1 April–1 October smoking/open-fire ban, but the run has no ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind/plume, visitor presence, access, firewater, suppression or closure state.
findings.action: Add selectable local nature-fire and external-smoke cases using versioned land cover/fuel, explicit ignition/perimeter, event-valid weather/moisture/spread, presence ranges, access/firewater, warning/closure and suppression state. A ban is prevention context, not evidence of zero fire or containment.

findings.summary: Two broad neighbourhoods and a repeated rank cannot represent island hazard pathways.
findings.evidence: Seven active single hazards plus wildfire rank Verspreide huizen first and the village second at T+24; compound repeats this. The same two polygons cannot resolve village residents, Banckspolder, protected versus outer-dike land, dune shelter, freshwater sites, ferry harbour, beaches, forest and moving visitors.
findings.action: Replace the shared local multiplier with full official hazard/support polygons and exposed objects. If finer privacy-safe exposure is unavailable, render municipal impact or bounded ranges without a precise two-area order and declare spatial support/NoData.

findings.summary: Off-island acute care and assisted evacuation are absent from Facilities and Mobility.
findings.evidence: RIVM has no local acute department; mainland 24/7 hospitals are at least 37.183 km straight-line away across water. KNRM examples show rescue-boat/helicopter patient transfer is possible, while municipal guidance promises special transport categories but supplies no live resource/capacity. Generic Facilities/Mobility decimals omit huisarts/ambulance, weather/tide, transfer, hospital acceptance and return logistics.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate local primary-care, ambulance, KNRM/helicopter activation, pickup/transfer route, mainland ED acceptance/diversion and backup/supply state. Record assisted-transport assignments and recipients privacy-safely; callable or historic operation never guarantees current capacity.

findings.summary: Exact eight-service values have no island topology, operator state or stock evidence.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 emits eight exact availabilities from Drainage 0.277130 to Gas 0.661721. Twenty-three capacity-null water points, a mainland grid-planning sample, eight antennas, three education records, local stops and facility registers provide no energy landing/feeder, fuel/gas, freshwater, sewer, backhaul, shelter, food/medicine stock, damage, backup, crews or restoration commitments.
findings.action: Keep public records affectsSimulation=false and suppress operator-looking decimals. Integrate safe authorized aggregates where available; otherwise use transparent versioned island zones/ranges with uncertainty and manual overrides retaining author, scope, timestamp and expiry.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration and recovery ignore island shelter, access and resource constraints.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct forcing clears by T+72 but leaves 143 affected and exact degraded services; compound worsens to 635 affected and Facilities 0.346024. Official 2026 evidence says rapid evacuation is nearly impossible, high-ground shelter lacks basic utilities/medical support and post-storm rescue is complex. No action/resource ledger explains warning, shelter, ferry, defence, water, care, fire, repair or resupply.
findings.action: Require T+0/6/12/24/48/72 incident/action/resource records with authority/owner, target, trigger, prerequisite, route, crew/vessel/material/fuel/water/stock, start/end, state, valid time and uncertainty. Only confirmed actions change recovery; missing state remains Unknown and 72 hours is not a restoration deadline.

findings.summary: Current policy disputes, defence standards, schedules, observations and synthetic results need explicit evidence separation.
findings.evidence: The UI can combine 2025 defence reporting, a 2026 proposed norm change and unresolved strengthening, current fire restrictions, ferry schedules, old/current registers and synthetic T+72 values. No GM0088 Waterinfo/KNMI/NDW observation exists in the bounded snapshot; absence is coverage, not safe/normal/open. The legacy flood value is liable to be mistaken for measured metres.
findings.action: Attach publisher, dataset/version, retrieval, issue/valid/event time, evidence class, lifecycle/proposal status, licence, spatial support, coverage, uncertainty, affectsSimulation and NoData beside every map/card/export. Never treat a proposal as effective law or normalized flood stress as measured depth.

corrections.summary: Add the Lauwersoog ferry and emergency maritime/air modes to the Schiermonnikoog lifeline graph.
corrections.validation: GM0088 no longer has a misleading zero-edge network: ferry terminal/channel/vessel, valid departures, tide/weather/navigability, passenger/freight/medical capacity and mainland onward routes are explicit. KNRM/helicopter require separate activation; missing state renders Unknown rather than open/available.

corrections.summary: Replace generic coastal precision with selected sandy-dune, Wadden-dike and outer-dike cases.
corrections.validation: Without a compatible expert-selected case, GM0088 direct coastal impact is Unknown/unsupported rather than 1.798438. Fixtures distinguish outer-dike salt marsh from protected-core failure and retain boundary level/datum, wind/waves, defence state, footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, probability, edition, CRS/resolution, licence and NoData.

corrections.summary: Add privacy-safe visitor/activity exposure and hazard-specific island geometry, including nature fire.
corrections.validation: CBS residents remain authoritative while event-time visitor/accommodation/ferry/workforce ranges remain separate and uncertain. Coastal, pluvial, heat and fire allocations use eligible full polygons/objects; unrelated hazards cannot silently share the two-neighbourhood rank and annual visitors are never treated as concurrent.

corrections.summary: Model aggregate freshwater, energy/telecom, shelter, stock and acute-care dependencies without inventing sensitive topology.
corrections.validation: Water state identifies local lens/abstraction/treatment/storage, quality, power and visitor demand or explicit Unknown; other lifelines show evidence-backed island landing/feed/backup/stock and medical transfer/acceptance ranges. All 23 capacity nulls and public planning/register fields remain non-operational.

corrections.summary: Implement an evidence-aware Unknown-first island action and resource ledger for T+0 through T+72.
corrections.validation: Warning, tourist accounting, high-ground shelter, assisted transport, defence, ferry/harbour, freshwater, medical evacuation, nature fire, utilities and resupply show authority, trigger, assignment, route/resource, state and valid time; only confirmed actions affect trajectories and missing facts remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish island electricity, gas/fuel, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, shelter, care or supply topology, live state, backup endurance, crews, vessels, inventories or restoration estimates.

No selected Wetterskip/RWS/WMCN/LIWO event establishes North Sea/Wadden level, wind/waves, sandy/dike failure or overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. No selected case is not a safety finding.
The 2026 proposed defence-norm change and disputed project consequences are not treated as settled law or current defence condition; policy lifecycle must be monitored.
All 23 HWH asset capacities are null and the registry lacks complete sewer/hydraulic connectivity, settings, maintenance, power, backup and event state.
The freshwater lens is strategically critical, but public evidence does not provide incident-time level, salinity, abstraction/treatment, storage, contamination, power or emergency distribution.

Ferry timetable/concession, zero NWB routes and 24 local stops do not establish tide/weather-dependent operation, vessel/berth availability, freight/passenger/medical capacity, mainland onward access or recovery.
KNRM and municipal sources establish callable/rescue possibilities, not guaranteed rescue-boat/helicopter/ambulance availability, weather limits, patient capacity or hospital acceptance.
Approximately 300,000 annual visitors cannot be converted to concurrent exposure; current accommodation, campsite, day-visitor, worker and ferry-queue occupancy is unavailable.
Two CBS neighbourhoods cannot resolve protected versus outer-dike areas, dunes, forest, beach/kwelder, freshwater, harbour, shelters or moving visitors without finer authoritative support.

One Liander planning sample, eight antennas and three education records are not island-wide outage, backhaul, shelter, occupancy or operational evidence; sensitive topology must not be reconstructed publicly.
No bounded local Waterinfo, KNMI, NDW, camera or acute-care record means NoData/coverage, not normal weather/water, open routes, safe conditions or available treatment.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not observations, forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and island authorities review the case.
This audit covers only 72 hours; flood recovery, salinisation/freshwater impacts, isolation, nature recovery and infrastructure repair can persist substantially longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Fryslân, Wetterskip, Rijkswaterstaat, VRF and each Wadden municipality should define expert-selected sandy-dune, Wadden-dike, outer-dike and rainfall cases with boundary, defence, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData.

Province, IenW/RWS, WPD, municipalities, mainland transport partners and emergency services should add ferry/channel/terminal and emergency marine/air connections as valid-time, capacity-bearing, non-road lifelines.

Wadden municipalities, CBS/province, ferry/accommodation partners and safety regions should define privacy-safe visitor/day-type occupancy ranges without converting annual tourism totals to concurrent people.

Vitens, island municipalities and water authorities should review publishable freshwater-lens, treatment/storage, power/backup, salinity/quality and emergency-distribution aggregates without exposing sensitive topology.

VRF, municipalities and nature managers should review dune/forest/grass fire and smoke cases, seasonal restrictions, visitor warning/closure, access, firefighting water, suppression and medical evacuation.

Fryslân partners should turn high-ground shelter and 72-hour preparedness into typed activation-gated actions/resources for utilities, water, food, medicine, vulnerable people, tourists, ferry isolation, repair and mainland rescue; policy, observation, forecast, live state, synthetic assumption and Unknown must remain distinct.
